To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The dimerization of phosphine-stabilized silylenes via silylene insertions into SiX (X = H, Cl) σ bonds was studied by means of DFT calculations.
phosphine-stabilized hydro- and chlorosilylenes 2 a,b undergo an unique reversible dimerization via insertion into SiH and SiCl bonds, respectively.
phosphine stabilized hydro-and chloro-silylene dimerize via silylene insertions into Si(II)-H and Si(III)-Cl σ-bonds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structure elucidation, and reactivity of phosphine-stabilized silylenes, in particular, their unique dimerization reaction via silylene-insertion into SiH and SiCl σ-bonds.
the synthesis of new phosphorus-containing compounds with the aim of gaining insight into their structures and reactivity.
the synthesis and the characterization of novel phosphine-stabilized silylenes, their reactivity, their coordination chemistry as well as their application as precursors for new materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the silylene insertion reaction into a SiH σ-bond is a reversible process and the dimerization of silylenes is not necessarily a thermodynamically favored reaction.
the silylene dication is not a stable species, but rather a transition state in the dimerization process.
the silylene insertion is a general reaction for phosphine-stabilized silylenes and is reversible at room-temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dimerization reaction of phosphine stabilized Si(II) compounds can be divided into three types: 1) classical dimerization to a disilane; 2) dimerization via insertion of Si(II) into Si(II)-X σ-bonds; 3) dimerization of Si(II)-H via insertion of Si-H bond.

the phosphine stabilized silylenes 2 a,b can be reversibly dimerized at room temperature by insertion into Si(II)-X σ-bonds, which is in contrast to the classical dimerization of silylenes to disilenes.
phosphine stabilized silylenes (PSs) are very reactive species and can react with various substrates, such as alkenes and alkynes to form various silylenes and silyne complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phosphine-stabilized hydro- and chlorosilylenes can be reversibly dimerized by silylene insertion reactions, which is contrary to the common knowledge of the silylene chemistry.
the silylenes (1 a,b) are able to insert themselves into the SiCl and SiH σ-bonds of the dimer (2 a or 2 b), which is in contrast to the classical dimerization of silylenes.
